scalars.analysis/core/results/hrv_freq/__attrs__: Welch PSD of the valid RR intervals resampled at 20 Hz (cubic spline on their true times; Hann, 75 % overlap, ≈0.02 Hz resolution); VLF / LF / HF = absolute band powers (ms²), LFn / HFn = LF or HF / (LF + HF) (Task Force n.u.); the PSD plot shows this same spectrum
scalars.analysis/core/results/intervals/__attrs_: mean preceding RR of the ensemble
scalars.analysis/frequency/__attrs__/method: Welch PSD of the valid RR intervals resampled at 20 Hz (cubic spline on their true times; Hann, 75 % overlap, ≈0.02 Hz resolution); VLF / LF / HF = absolute band powers (ms²), LFn / HFn = LF or HF / (LF + HF) (Task Force n.u.); the PSD plot shows this same spectrum
scalars.autonomic/beats/__attrs__/calibration_no: ks = 3, kp = 12: rat (SHR) calibration of Candia-Rivera et al., J Physiol 2025 (inflection of the rest-vs-dobutamine Wilcoxon Z over k = 1-20). NOT validated in mice. CSI/CPI are linear in ks/kp (dCSI = -dD + ks*dSD2, dCPI = dD + kp*dSD1), so they can be re-calibrated on a mouse cohort from per-event deltas of D, SD1 and SD2.
scalars.autonomic/beats/__attrs__/method_note: Schafer-Strimmer shrinkage covariance (robustCovHRV.m: variances shrunk toward their median, correlation toward 0) with 5 % trimmed-mean CCD -- the method the paper text describes. The published rat function (compute_CSI_CVI_rat.m) uses plain cov() instead. A window in which either Poincaré coordinate is constant (zero RR variance, e.g. very low HRV at a coarse sampling rate) has an undefined correlation and is withheld whole -- SD1, SD2 and CCD NaN (robustCovHRV.m returns NaN there).
